title: Yom Kippur
hookLine: the Day of Atonement: Jews fast, pray and ask forgiveness

cards: No breakfast. No lunch. No coffee.

A whole community, from evening to evening, puts down food and drink and spends the day in prayer. And the subject of all those hours isn't a victory or a harvest. It's what went wrong this year, and how to set it right.
Earlier on this path came the Days of Awe, the time for making amends. This is the day they end on. Its name, in Hebrew, is Yom Kippur.
In English: the Day of Atonement.

teach.b: First, the text. Leviticus gives the day its purpose, in the King James words: "For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD." Clean.
The day is a washing, not a punishment. Second, how it's kept.

Leviticus also says: "there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls". Jewish tradition reads afflicting the soul as fasting and other kinds of going without.
The body's ordinary comforts step aside so the attention can go somewhere else. Third, the order.

Twice on this path, on days nine hundred forty-two and nine hundred seventy-eight, came the Mishnah's rule: the day atones for wrongs between a person and God, but for wrongs between people, not until you've made peace with the person you wronged.
So the real work of Yom Kippur often starts before it: phone calls, apologies, asking forgiveness face to face.
Fourth, what it adds up to: a cleansing before God, a fast that clears the ordinary out of the way, and peace made with people first.
The day isn't only about being sorry.
It's about coming back into right relationship, with God, with each other, and with the person you mean to be.

how: On Yom Kippur Jews fast from evening to evening and spend much of the day in synagogue prayer, including confession; in the days before it, people seek out those they've wronged to ask forgiveness.

games.q: the Day of Atonement — tap the pairs.

s: Leviticus describes the day as a cleansing
"to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD."
the Mishnah says the day atones for everything, even wrongs you never made right
wrongs between people need the other person's forgiveness first.
Leviticus says nothing about how the day is kept
"ye shall afflict your souls", which Jewish tradition reads as fasting.

games.q: it's the week before Yom Kippur. you wronged a friend this year. what does the Mishnah say about the day atoning for that?
o: the day atones for it automatically.
the day atones only after you make peace with your friend.
only fasting harder can atone for it.
games.why: for wrongs between people, the day doesn't atone until you've made peace with the person you wronged.

practice: Ask one question and let it stay open: where did I miss the mark this year? Not where others did; where I did.
Let one or two answers come without arguing, then ask a second: is there someone I need to speak to before anything else can be set right? If you pray, you can bring both answers into your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Yom Kippur. The Day of Atonement, when Jews fast, pray and ask forgiveness, of God and, first, of one another. Today's word.
